summary: httpz-requests ships a Telegram-controlled remote shell agent
details: Package `httpz-requests` presents itself under an HTTP-client-style name but its actual purpose is a Telegram-driven remote administration agent on the installer's host. `__init__.py` imports `start_bot` from a shipped compiled module `bot.so`; sibling Cython-compiled modules `handlers.so`, `core.so`, and `obfuscate.so` receive messages via the Telegram Bot API and execute them as shell commands on the machine that installed and started the agent. The package ships only `.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so` binaries with no Python source, and its README states that commands are encoded before execution so they do not appear in process listings or logs. Package metadata is placeholder (`Aapka Naam <you@example.com>`, repository URL `https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/httpz-requests`), and the package name resembles an HTTP-requests library while the actual functionality is a remote-shell agent, creating typosquat-style confusion for developers searching for HTTP tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
